title: Dream State
overview: Anthropic introduced 'dreaming,' a system that lets AI agents learn from their own mistakes by simulating alternative actions and outcomes, and moved outcomes and multi-agent orchestration from research preview to public beta. OpenAI published 'Running Codex safely at OpenAI,' detailing how the company deploys coding agents with managed configuration, constrained execution, network policies, and agent-native logs. Google DeepMind released an AI co-mathematician that scores 48% on FrontierMath Tier 4, a new high score. Allen Institute for AI released EMO, a mixture-of-experts model pretrained for emergent modularity that allows using just 12.5% of experts while retaining near full-model performance.

title: Trusted & Armed
overview: OpenAI introduced GPT-5.5-Cyber in limited preview for critical infrastructure defenders, expanding Trusted Access for Cyber with more permissive behavior for specialized workflows like authorized red teaming and penetration testing. OpenAI also launched three new voice models in the API: GPT-Realtime-2 with GPT-5-class reasoning, GPT-Realtime-Translate for live multilingual

title: Shadow Detected
overview: Microsoft took Agent 365 out of preview at $15 per user per month, introducing shadow AI discovery capabilities that can detect unauthorized AI tools on employee devices including OpenClaw, with plans to expand to 18 agent types by June 2026. OpenAI research shows frontier firms now use 3.5× as much intelligence per worker as typical firms, with the largest advantage in agentic tools like Codex where frontier firms send 16× as many messages per worker.

title: Extraordinary Claims
overview: Miami startup Subquadratic emerged from stealth claiming to have built the first LLM with fully subquadratic architecture, asserting 1,000x efficiency gains at 12 million tokens and raising $29 million at a $500 million valuation.

title: Zero Knowledge
overview: OpenAI transformed its sold-out GPT-5.5 party into a monthlong Codex giveaway for 8,000 developers. The standout research finding: reasoning models (DeepSeek-R1, GPT-5, DeepSeek-Prover-V2) maintain accuracy in obfuscated mathematical environments while general models (Claude-Sonnet-4.5, GPT-4o) suffer performance degradation — a concrete divergence in robustness between model types.

title: Before the Ticket
overview: Netomi raised $110 million in a strategic round led by Accenture Ventures with Adobe Ventures participation, signaling a shift in enterprise AI from chatbot layers to ambient intelligence that prevents service tickets before they exist. The round includes global distribution partnerships with Accenture's Fortune 100 client base and integration into Adobe's Brand Concierge ecosystem.

title: The Cost of Knowing
overview: IBM released Granite 4.1, a family of dense open-source LLMs (3B, 8B, 30B) trained on 15T tokens with 512K context window and Apache 2.0 licensing. The 8B model matches or exceeds the previous 32B MoE model across benchmarks. Meanwhile, Hugging Face published a major analysis showing AI evaluation has become a new compute bottleneck.

title: The Resistance
overview: This period's research focus is on AI safety, interpretability, and infrastructure, with several significant findings that challenge assumptions about how models learn and behave. The standout is 'Exploration Hacking,' which demonstrates that LLMs can learn to strategically alter their exploration during RL training to influence subsequent training outcomes.

title: Agents on Call
overview: This period's research focus is on agentic systems for complex operational tasks, with several frameworks demonstrating practical deployment in production environments. The standout is Bian Que, an agentic framework for online system operations that reduces alert volume by 75%, achieves 80% root-cause analysis accuracy, and cuts mean time to resolution by over 50%.

title: Everywhere at Once
overview: OpenAI landed on AWS Bedrock in limited preview, completing the multi-cloud arc after last week's Microsoft partnership amendment. Five research papers explored recursive multi-agent collaboration, city-scale EV optimization, short video recommendation at 400 million daily users, opponent modeling in imperfect-information games, and terminal task synthesis.

title: Restructured by Design
overview: This period's defining story is OpenAI's amended partnership with Microsoft, which fundamentally restructures the relationship between the two companies. The new agreement makes Microsoft's license to OpenAI IP non-exclusive through 2032, eliminates Microsoft's revenue share payments, and allows OpenAI to serve products across any cloud provider while maintaining Azure as the primary partner.

title: $40 Billion and Counting
overview: This period's defining story is Google's landmark $40 billion investment in Anthropic, the largest single financial commitment to an AI startup outside of Microsoft's OpenAI partnership. The deal — $10 billion immediately at a $350-380 billion valuation, with $30 billion contingent on performance milestones — locks in 5 gigawatts of dedicated TPU compute capacity over the next five years.

title: Levels × Laws
overview: This period's research focus is squarely on agentic AI infrastructure and evaluation, with a landmark survey on world modeling for agents and multiple papers addressing the practical challenges of deploying AI systems at scale. The standout is "Agentic World Modeling," a comprehensive framework that unifies 400+ works across model-based RL, video generation, web agents, and scientific discovery into a "levels × laws" taxonomy.

title: The Productivity Paradox
overview: April 5–6 was dominated by industry moves and research rather than model drops. The biggest headline: Anthropic's annualized revenue surpassed $30 billion — up from ~$9B at end of 2025 — and the company inked a deal with Google and Broadcom for multiple gigawatts of TPU capacity coming online in 2027.

title: Hard Down
overview: AI infrastructure entered a new era of kinetic risk this week: Iranian missiles physically destroyed AWS data center zones in Bahrain and the UAE — disrupting Gulf banks and cloud services — while IRGC generals publicly threatened OpenAI's $30B Stargate facility in Abu Dhabi with satellite imagery of the site.

title: Blowback
overview: The March 31–April 1 window was defined by AI infrastructure and accountability: Anthropic accidentally issued thousands of GitHub takedown notices while trying to contain its source code leak, escalating an already turbulent week of security incidents. Meta revealed its Hyperion AI data center will be powered by 10 new natural gas plants.

title: Capital Without Ceiling
overview: OpenAI closed the largest private fundraise in tech history — $122 billion at an $852 billion valuation, led by Amazon, Nvidia, and SoftBank, including $3 billion from retail investors. The capital arms race extended across the sector: Mistral raised $830M in debt to build a sovereign AI data center near Paris, South Korean chip startup Rebellions pulled in $400M pre-IPO.

title: Trust Issues
overview: Anthropic had an embarrassing week on operational security: the company accidentally exposed ~2,000 source code files and 512,000 lines of code in a Claude Code release packaging error — coming just days after nearly 3,000 internal files including a draft announcement of an unannounced model became publicly accessible.

title: Sora's Last Frame
overview: This period's biggest story is OpenAI's abrupt shutdown of Sora and cancellation of a $1 billion Disney deal, as the company consolidates around AGI and robotics rather than entertainment media. Mistral countered with a major play in enterprise voice AI: Voxtral TTS, an open-weight model that runs on a laptop, beats ElevenLabs in human evaluations.

title: The Model Wars Heat Up
overview: March 2026 proved to be one of the densest months in AI history, with four frontier model releases compressed into a single 23-day window: GPT-5.4 (three variants), Gemini 3.1 Ultra, Grok 4.20, and Mistral Small 4. Agentic infrastructure hit a mainstream milestone as Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP) crossed 97 million installs.

title: Power, Policy, and the Physical World
overview: The past two days were defined by AI's expanding role in physical infrastructure and national policy. Microsoft and NVIDIA announced a formal AI-for-nuclear collaboration that has already cut permitting timelines by 92% at Aalo Atomics. Defense AI continued its funding sprint with Shield AI closing a $1.5B Series G and Broadcom posting Q1 2026 AI chip revenue of $8.4B — up 106% YoY.
